request: Write one complete bilingual technical reference chapter, English followed by pt-BR, for esp-hal command parsing at the supplied exact revision. Audience: maintainers of CI command handling. Scope: parseHilCommand, parseTestSizeCommand, their local parsing/classification helpers, chips.json configuration and the selected dispatch/help integration boundaries. Explain exact matching/first-line behavior, normalized chips versus original names, deduplication, classification precedence, help versus error precedence, quick/full/explicit selection, canonical packages, all output fields/types, null/error results and distinction from authorization or actual workflow execution. Preserve identifiers and negation in both languages. Give one source-derived illustrative call/output example per API in each language with identical code bytes across languages; label examples unexecuted. Include corresponding FAQs: does parser success authorize dispatch, what determines chip order, and does help override invalid options? Cite supplied file names/line ranges near claims. Lifecycle action ADD applies only to an isolated proposed reference chapter. Do not edit external repositories, invoke GitHub APIs, send comments, trigger workflows, execute project source/tests or claim runtime test success. State uncertainties, especially runtime expression semantics beyond the selected source. Apply unchanged G1-G9 technical gates with independent procedure limits explicit.
context_delivery_policy: References are evaluator-only. Model context must be a frozen source-only envelope of full parser, chips JSON and selected line-numbered workflow ranges; actual token-fit remains unverified until authorized runtime.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: SOCS preserves chips.json order; QUICK includes entries with truthy quick configuration.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: normalizeChip lowercases, removes every hyphen/underscore, adds esp32 unless already present, then validates membership in SOCS.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: commandWords reads only the first physical line before trim, uses a case-insensitive anchored command regex, and splits arguments on whitespace, comma or equals. A command on a later line is not read.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: NAME permits ASCII letters/digits/underscore/colon/hyphen; listed test/package flags are ignored words; HIL aliases map test/tests to hil-test and radio to hil-test-radio.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: sortWords classifies known flags, chips, keywords and packages before unknown-option, chip-like and invalid-name errors, then names; its add helper deduplicates destination lists.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: Keyword/package comparison is lowercase, but accepted test/example name values preserve the original word; do not promise all tokens are lowercased.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: parseHilCommand recognizes /hil or /test, returns null for no match, then returns the base help result for no words or help keyword before returning sorted errors. Empty arrays are truthy in the find(Boolean) match.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: full/all selects every SOCS entry. quick unions configured quick entries with explicitly selected chips. No chips yields a descriptive error. Output chip order follows SOCS, not user order.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: selector becomes full for full/all, otherwise quick only when quick was requested and every explicit chip is in QUICK, otherwise the selected chip string. tests joins names with commas.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: Successful HIL output has help/error/chips/selector/tests/package; package is all when multiple canonical packages were selected, otherwise first canonical package or hil-test default.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: SIZE_PACKAGES maps examples/example to empty default and qa-test/qa to qa-test.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: parseTestSizeCommand returns null for nonmatch and accumulates errors for sorting, missing examples, missing chips and more than one canonical package; it has no separate help result.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: Pinned configuration lists twelve chips; only esp32s3 and esp32c6 have quick:true. Read configuration, not prose alone, for the actual quick set.

needs: auth
    if: github.event_name == 'issue_comment' &&
      needs.auth.outputs.allowed == 'true' &&
      (startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/hil ') ||
      startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/test '))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6 # for `require`
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Resolve dispatch parameters
        id: mode
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          # A command that can't be run is answered by `hil-help`.
          script: |
            const { parseHilCommand } = require('./.github/scripts/hil-parse.js');
            const res = parseHilCommand(context.payload.comment.body) || {};

            core.setOutput('selector', res.selector || '');
            core.setOutput('chips', res.chips || '');
            core.setOutput('tests', res.tests || '');
            core.setOutput('package', res.package || '');

      - name: Dispatch HIL
        if: steps.mode.outputs.chips != ''
reference_propositions.reference_proposition: HIL dispatch job requires issue_comment and auth.allowed true plus its literal command prefix conditions; it maps parser output to workflow outputs and gates actual dispatch on nonempty chips. Parser recognition alone does not authorize dispatch.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.quote:
hil-help:
    if: github.event_name == 'issue_comment' &&
      github.event.issue.pull_request &&
      (startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/hil') ||
      startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/test')) &&
      !startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/test-')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6 # for `require`
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Explain usage
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const { parseHilCommand, USAGE } = require('./.github/scripts/hil-parse.js');
            const res = parseHilCommand(context.payload.comment.body);
            if (!res || (!res.help && !res.error)) return;

            const login = context.payload.comment.user.login;
            const problem = res.error ? `@${login}, this command can't be run:\n${res.error}\n\n` : '';
            await github.rest.issues.createComment({
              ...context.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              body: problem + USAGE,
reference_propositions.reference_proposition: The separate HIL help job parses commands, returns when no help/error applies, otherwise prepares a usage/problem comment. This campaign never runs it or posts comments.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: Size dispatch also requires auth and its prefix condition; missing/error result prepares an explanatory comment and setFailed then returns. Successful chips are JSON-encoded for downstream outputs.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

reference_propositions.reference_proposition: The CommonJS exports are parseHilCommand, parseTestSizeCommand and USAGE; helper functions are local implementation details.
reference_propositions.method: Same-agent source/context review; composite reference unit, not independent atomic metric.

negative_reference_claims.claim: Parser success authorizes any commenter to launch HIL.
HIL output chips preserve user input order.
All names are converted to lowercase.
A matching command on the second physical line is parsed.
The /test-size command is a /test command to parseHilCommand.
help plus an unknown option always returns the unknown-option error.
Size parsing combines examples and qa-test as one package.
HIL chips and size chips have the same output type.
The quick set is hardcoded in normalizeChip.
These workflow actions and HIL tests passed during this campaign.
